name: Estates administration
one_line: The practitioner-side apparatus for winding up the affairs of a person who has DIED - the death-and-authority record, the date-of-death valuation set, the death-tax account, the creditor notice, the estate accounts and the distribution to beneficiaries. Its distinct default is a DECEASED-AND-INSTANT anchor rather than the schema's client-and-matter anchor: the person the file is about is not the client, cannot be, and cannot consent, and every asset in the file is valued at one frozen instant instead of over a period. It is NOT activated by the word estate, by a will, by a death certificate, by a practice-area label, or by a deceased person's ordinary bank statements.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: REUSE OF AN EXISTING PROPOSAL, NOT A MINT. `subject_of_record` is already proposed by `clinical_practice` and is already carried in this schema's own anchor role_split; this row asks for nothing new except that the adjudication cover a subject who is DEAD. The canonical `client` key cannot carry it: in this family the client is the personal representative - an executor or administrator, alive, sometimes several, sometimes replaced mid-administration, sometimes a beneficiary and sometimes not - and the person whose affairs the file actually contains is the deceased, who is not a party to the retainer and never was. Minting `deceased`, `estate_of`, `testator` or `decedent` would be exactly the synonym mint the brief forbids, since the concept is the one `subject_of_record` already names. 00's role rule is the general licence: "The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type" - and here the same surname routinely occupies the client slot, the subject slot and the beneficiary slot inside one folder.
proposed_fields.preferred_resolution: R1c adjudicates the key once across clinical_practice, nonprofit and law_practice. This row asks for ONE condition and it is stricter than the schema anchor's: `destination_eligible` must be FALSE, and unlike the anchor's client level it must not become eligible on user approval either, for a reason specific to death. A folder named for a living client discloses that a representation exists; a folder named for a dead person additionally writes a bereavement, and the surviving family who share the machine did not choose that label. If canonical_fields cannot express a per-schema eligibility difference, the ban belongs in the template contract, which is the same shape of problem the anchor raised for `client`.
proposed_fields.why: The estate anchor. Without it the family has no way to say that the file is ABOUT someone who is not its client, which is the one structural fact that separates this row from every other row on the schema.

deterministic: PRECONDITION - the schema's own two-leg default still binds and is not weakened here: an exact matter or file reference repeated across artefacts, plus at least one artefact whose labelled slots separate a practitioner or firm role from a client role. Nothing below overrides it. A lay executor's own probate bundle satisfies every signal in this list and is still NOT this row, because there is no practitioner side; it is `legal.personal-legal-matters`. The deletion test the schema inherits applies unchanged: strike every person name, every firm name and every document-type word, and if no structure survives, nothing fires.

THE DEATH-AND-AUTHORITY PAIR, and it is what makes this row a template rather than a repetition of the schema default. A THREE-role structure where the default requires two: an artefact whose own labelled slots carry (i) a deceased-person slot with a DATE OF DEATH, and (ii) an authority slot naming a personal representative - executor, executrix, administrator, administratrix, personal representative - together with the instrument that appoints them, a will clause or a grant. The default's client-and-practitioner pair is present but is not the anchor; the anchor is the third role, the person the file is about, who is dead. Read through 00's direct path, "a labeled form field".

THE DATE-OF-DEATH VALUATION SLOT - the family's sharpest signal and the one that fires where the schema default cannot. A letter, statement or certificate from a bank, registrar, insurer, valuer or land agent whose own labelled line reads as a value AS AT a single stated date, that date being a death date rather than a statement period end, addressed to a personal representative or to the practitioner acting for one. These artefacts frequently carry NO matter reference and NO role pair, so the schema's two-leg default fails on them outright; they are recognisable only by the valuation-instant slot plus the addressee role. The same slot repeats as a COLUMN HEADER on the schedule that aggregates them.

AN ASSET-AND-LIABILITY SCHEDULE AT ONE INSTANT: a table with one row per asset carrying a description, a holding institution or location, a holding size, a value at the death date, and a sole-or-joint or beneficial-share column, followed by a liabilities block that characteristically includes funeral account rows. Read through 00's spreadsheet path - "Spreadsheets such as XLSX, XLS, CSV, TSV, ODS, and Numbers exports should yield workbook or file metadata, sheet names, column headers, visible cell values, table-like regions, formulas only when useful, and dates or identifiers from labeled cells". The discriminating evidence is the SINGLE-INSTANT column, not the presence of money: a portfolio valuation with a period, a range or a series of dates is finance's on finance's own evidence.

A DEATH-TAX ACCOUNT STRUCTURE: a labelled form whose own schedules enumerate asset classes at one instant plus lifetime-gift, relief, exemption and domicile schedules keyed to a death date, with a computation that closes to a single liability and a clearance or determination response - IHT400 with IHT403, IHT405, IHT406 and IHT421 in England and Wales, Form 706 with its lettered schedules and Form 5173 clearance in the United States, and their equivalents elsewhere. It has NO tax year and no period, which is the structural break from an ordinary return.

AN ESTATE ACCOUNT STRUCTURE: a statement whose own section headings separate a CAPITAL account from an INCOME account and from a DISTRIBUTION account, opening from the date-of-death asset total, running administration receipts and payments, and closing to a residue divided in fractions or percentages among named beneficiaries, with an approval or release line for the personal representative. No other artefact on this schema has this three-ledger grammar.

A CREDITOR-NOTICE AND CLAIMS-PERIOD structure: a statutory advertisement or notice-to-creditors record pairing the deceased's name, last address and date of death with a claim deadline and a place of publication, filed beside the proof of publication. A claims register with one row per claimant, claim amount, admitted-or-rejected decision and payment date belongs to the same structure.

A DISTRIBUTION-AND-RELEASE structure: one document or one table row per beneficiary carrying an entitlement expressed as a share of residue or a named legacy, interim and final payment lines, and a receipt, release, assent or transfer acknowledgement. The FRACTIONAL-SHARE-OF-A-WHOLE grammar is the signal; a payment run with per-payee amounts and no share denominator is finance's.

AN INTESTACY-ENTITLEMENT structure: a worked statement deriving who takes and in what share from a family tree and a statutory order, usually beside a family-tree or heirship diagram and sometimes a genealogist's report. It is the no-will mirror of the will-construction note and belongs to the same anchor.
needs_llm: Deciding whether a stated date on a valuation letter is a DEATH date or a period end. The two are typographically identical and the difference decides the row. The surrounding sentence, the addressee role and the presence of a death certificate or grant reference in the same folder settle it; nothing in the number does.

Separating a deceased person's ordinary pre-death financial run from the administration set that follows it. The same institution, the same account and the same account holder appear on both sides of the death date; only the addressee role and the valuation-instant framing change.
Reading a will or codicil for whether the file is a LIFETIME planning artefact or an ADMINISTRATION artefact. The instrument is identical; the discriminator is entirely in what surrounds it.

Reading an estate-account-shaped document for whether it accounts for a bounded administration or for one year of a continuing trust. The ledger grammar is shared; the period-versus-instant framing and the governing-instrument reference separate them.

Resolving whether a contentious document - a claim against the estate, a will challenge, a family-provision application - is administration work product or a proceeding. If it carries a tribunal caption or an execution block it is `legal`'s on `legal`'s evidence, and the sibling proceeding rows are the practitioner-side home.

Deciding whether a chattels photograph was taken as valuation evidence or as an ordinary family photograph of the same object. Only an accompanying valuer's schedule item reference decides it, and where that is absent the file stays photos'.
never_alone: THE WORD ESTATE. It is the family's cheapest false positive and it is ambiguous three ways in ordinary filenames: an estate agent's particulars, a real-estate transaction, and the annual accounts of a living family settlement all carry it. `Estate agent valuation - 14 Elm Road.pdf` contains the word twice over and has no death in it at all.

A DEATH CERTIFICATE ALONE. It is `identity`'s artefact on `identity`'s evidence, and a person may keep a parent's death certificate for decades with no administration, no practitioner and no estate file anywhere. It is a co-activation member, never an activator.

A WILL OR CODICIL ALONE. An executed testamentary instrument is `legal`'s on the bound-party-and-execution structure, and while its testator lives it is `legal.estate-planning`'s. Nothing about the instrument itself says whether the testator has died.

THE WORD PROBATE, GRANT, EXECUTOR, ADMINISTRATOR, DECEASED, DEC'D, ESTATE OF or LATE in a filename, alone or in combination with any other struck token. These are document-type and role words and the schema's rule that a role name can never carry a template applies to them without exception.

A DECEASED PERSON'S BANK, BROKERAGE OR PENSION STATEMENT ALONE. It is structurally indistinguishable from any other account holder's statement; death is not visible in it. Finance owns it on its own evidence and finance is a safety domain whose protection runs first.

A SURNAME SHARED ACROSS FILES. The deceased, the executor and several beneficiaries commonly share one surname, so a family name is the weakest possible bridge here and is exactly the shape 00 rules out for organisations - "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization."

A PRACTICE-AREA LABEL - a firm's private client, wills and probate, or trusts and estates department name on a letterhead or in a folder path. A department is an organisation name and cannot activate anything.
A DATE THAT IS MERELY OLD OR MERELY REPEATED. The valuation instant matters because a labelled slot says what it is, not because several documents happen to share a date.

proposed_context_terms: as at the date of death
work_types: death registration record and initial asset and liability enquiry
date-of-death valuation request and valuation response
will, codicil, office copy and will-construction note
grant application, statement of truth or oath, and lodgement record
death-tax account, schedules, computation and clearance
asset collection, encashment, transfer and re-registration record
creditor notice, claims register and liability settlement record
estate bank account, cash book and administration receipts and payments
interim and final estate accounts and residue computation
beneficiary correspondence, entitlement statement and deed of variation
assent, transfer, legacy payment and distribution receipt or release
continuing trust, life interest and minority-interest handover record
estate income tax and administration-period return record
claim against the estate and contentious-probate correspondence
file closure, retention and papers-to-personal-representative record
grouping_reasons: The DECEASED-AND-INSTANT pair repeated across artefacts: one deceased-person identity slot together with one date of death. This is the family's anchor and it is stronger than a surname because it is two slots that must agree, and 00 requires an anchor at all - "It should not form a supported group when there is no valid anchor".
The allocated matter or file reference, inherited unchanged from the schema default and still the primary anchor where it is present.
A grant, probate registry or court file reference repeated on the tax account, the asset schedule and the asset-collection correspondence.
The designated estate or executors' account number repeated across the cash book, the statements and the distribution schedule.

An exact schedule item identifier carried from the asset schedule to the valuation letter to the tax schedule to the distribution row. This is the family's most useful fine-grained bridge and the one that must never copy a fact: the item number groups, it does not label.
MEMBERSHIP NEVER COPIES. Joining an estate group writes no fact onto the member - not the deceased, not the date of death, not a share, not a value, not a legal entitlement, and not a folder path.

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT - the schema declares no fields under PR-6, so no dimension may branch on anything, and the co-activated `legal` and `finance` readings are safety domains, so "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains" and no deep template unlocks from that activation. WHAT THE RECOMMENDATION WOULD BE, AND HOW IT DIFFERS FROM THE SCHEMA'S DEFAULT PARAGRAPH - this is the leg of the node test this row is measured on, and it differs in three ways rather than one. FIRST, THE CLIENT LEVEL IS STRUCK, NOT SEEDED-INELIGIBLE. The schema's default seeds a client level ineligible but allows it on explicit user approval where a corpus genuinely spans several clients. Here it is wrong even when approved, for a reason that is not privacy: the client is the personal representative, and personal representatives are plural, substitutable and sometimes themselves beneficiaries, so a client level would scatter one estate across co-executors and would file a dead person's affairs under a living person who is not their subject. SECOND, THE ANCHOR DIMENSION IS A SUBJECT, NOT A MATTER. The estate - the deceased together with the death date - is what every artefact in the file agrees on, including the many that carry no matter reference at all; the allocated file reference remains the safe DISPLAY label precisely because it does not name anyone. THIRD, THERE IS NO PERIOD LEVEL. The schema's default ends with a period level; an administration is one bounded episode measured from one instant, so a year level would cut it at an arbitrary point and would separate the date-of-death valuation from the distribution it feeds. Function - valuation, tax, collection, creditors, accounts, distribution, closure - then follows the estate, on 00's parent-before-child rule: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known", and an assent, a residue computation or a schedule item is meaningless without the estate it belongs to. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: the administration STAGE - pre-grant, grant, collection, distribution, closure - is a tempting level and is refused, because a stage is a lifecycle value and would move files as the matter progressed, which is the opposite of a durable destination. NOT TIME-FIRST, AND THIS ROW HAS TO SAY SO LOUDLY because it is the one row on the schema a naive detector would try it on: the corpus is saturated with one strongly agreeing date and looks capture-like, but the date is a VALUATION INSTANT, not a capture time, and 00's rule holds - "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." And whatever lands stays a recommendation the user may reverse or flatten.

collides_with.signal: THE SAME BYTES ON BOTH SIDES OF A DEATH, and the cleanest reciprocal in the family. Shared fixture: `Will and codicil - Margaret Ellis - 2019 - office copy.pdf`. THEIRS when the instrument sits in a lifetime planning set - a will beside a power of attorney, a letter of wishes, a trust deed, a nomination form - with no death date anywhere in the neighbourhood, and characteristically held by or for the testator themselves. MINE when the identical instrument arrives inside a practitioner file that also holds a death certificate, a grant application and a date-of-death schedule. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A DEATH DATE PLUS AN ADMINISTRATION APPARATUS, and it is never the instrument. Reciprocal, stated both ways: estate-planning must not claim a will that arrives with a death certificate and a valuation schedule; this row must not claim a will that arrives alone or with a living testator's planning bundle, however probate-shaped the filename. Provenance: inference.

THE LAY-EXECUTOR COLLISION - the threat to this row's existence, and it is resolved by the schema's precondition rather than by anything this template adds. Shared fixture: `Probate application and IHT205 - Mum's estate - my copy.pdf`. THEIRS whenever the holder is administering an estate personally: the death date, the asset schedule, the grant application and the tax account are all present, and none of them is practitioner-side evidence. MINE only where the schema's practitioner-and-client structure independently holds. Reciprocal: personal-legal-matters must not be displaced merely because a document is probate-shaped and structurally rich; this row must not annex a bereaved person's own paperwork on the strength of its structure. Note for R1c: this is the family's largest genuine coverage gap and it is recorded as NJ-EA-1 rather than solved by theft. Provenance: inference.

Shared fixtures: `Barclays - date of death balance - E Ellis - 14 March 2026.pdf` and the deceased's run of ordinary monthly statements. THEIRS on the institution-and-account structure, on its own evidence, and finance is a safety domain so its protection runs first - a dead account holder's statements are structurally indistinguishable from a living one's and death is not visible in them. MINE only on the valuation-instant slot addressed to a personal representative, and on the schedule that AGGREGATES across institutions - a document with no single institution or account of its own, which is precisely why finance cannot see it. Reciprocal: finance must not swallow the cross-institution asset schedule; this row must not claim a statement run because the account holder has died. Provenance: inference.

Shared fixture family: `IHT400 and schedules` beside `Final income tax return to date of death`. THEIRS on a tax_year or accounting-period structure - the deceased's final personal return and the administration-period returns both carry one, and both are genuinely tax-filings' even though they sit in the estate folder. MINE on the death-tax account, which has NO tax year at all: its schedules are keyed to a single death date, which is the structural break. Reciprocal: tax-filings must not claim an IHT or 706 account by the word tax; this row must not claim the final personal return by the words to date of death in its title. This seam matters because inventing a tax_year fact on a death-tax account would hand the whole file to the wrong row. Provenance: inference.

Shared fixture: the deceased's house. THEIRS for the sale file - contract, searches, enquiries, completion statement, transfer to a buyer - which is a conveyancing transaction whoever the seller is. MINE for the date-of-death valuation of the same property, and for the ASSENT transferring it to a beneficiary rather than selling it, which has no buyer, no price and no contract. Reciprocal: conveyancing must not claim the assent or the death valuation; this row must not claim the sale file merely because the seller is a personal representative. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: The commonest co-activation here and the reason this row can be narrow. One estate folder holds a sealed grant, an executed will and a deed of variation (`legal`, on the caption and execution structure) beside a valuation set, a tax account, estate accounts and a distribution schedule (this row, on the deceased-and-instant apparatus) - disjoint evidence, one folder, both schemas fieldless. `legal` is a safety domain so the protective ordering runs first. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

A death certificate, a surrendered passport and the personal representative's own identity verification are routine and mandatory members of an estate file. The identity documents are identity's and stay protected on its evidence; the verification record that lists them is this schema's. Membership never converts identity data into an estate fact. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

A registrar's or broker's date-of-death holding valuation is legitimately both: the holding, the institution and the security are brokerage evidence on brokerage's own structure, and the valuation-instant framing plus the personal-representative addressee is this row's. Two readings on one page, neither erasing the other, and finance's protection runs first. One-way here; R1c owes the reciprocal. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: Named first and it takes most of this family. The characteristic isolated file here is a document about a DEAD third party and their surviving family - a valuation letter, a death certificate, an entitlement statement, a page of estate accounts. 00 names this residual and this material together: "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts."

The home for this family's defining failure, which is a date whose meaning is unresolved - a valuation-shaped letter where nothing says whether the stated date is a death or a period end, and the trust-versus-administration accounts collision. "Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision."

The honest home for a standalone administration document that exposes no living third party and joins no group - a creditor notice, a proof of publication, a blank statement of truth. "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

Isolated transactional members are ordinary here: a probate registry fee receipt, a Gazette advertisement invoice, a funeral account, a courier confirmation for the will. "Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoice"
Password-protected and split practice-system exports and scanned estate bundles are ordinary and must not be forced open to improve classification. "Unsupported or Encrypted may hold"

role_split.why: THE FAMILY'S DEFINING SPLIT AND THE ONE THE SCHEMA DEFAULT DOES NOT HAVE. On every other row of this schema the client and the subject of the record are usually the same person; here they are NEVER the same person, by definition, because the subject is dead. The personal representative is the client and is alive; the deceased is the subject and cannot consent, instruct, object or be consulted; a beneficiary is neither, and may be a third party who does not yet know they are in the file. 00's general rule licenses the separation - "The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type" - and it bites unusually hard here because all three roles routinely carry the SAME SURNAME inside one folder. `subject_of_record` is pointed at clinical_practice because that is the row adjudicating the key; this row asks only that the adjudication reach a dead subject, and asks that both keys be destination-ineligible for this family. Provenance: inference; the underlying role-separation rule is design.

Inherited unchanged from the schema anchor rather than restated: the practitioner-and-client pair is what decides whether an estate file is this schema's at all or is the holder's own bereavement paperwork. This row adds one wrinkle for R1c - a personal representative is frequently a lay family member with no organisation name attached, so the client half of the pair here is a PERSON rather than a firm, and any resolution rule that expects an organisation string on both sides will fail on the commonest case in this family. Provenance: inference.

sensitivity_why: The strictest posture available, and it is argued on three grounds that are NOT the schema default's. The schema's argument is that the existence of a representation is itself disclosive; here that argument is partly FALSE and something worse replaces it. FIRST, EXISTENCE IS OFTEN PUBLIC AND THE CONTENTS NEVER ARE. A grant of representation is a public register entry in many jurisdictions and a creditor notice is a published advertisement, so the fact that an estate is being administered may be discoverable by anyone - but who was left out of the will, what the residue came to, which beneficiary took what share, and what the deceased owned are not, and they are all inside the same folder. The posture must therefore protect CONTENT even where the schema default would relax on publicity. SECOND, THE SUBJECT CANNOT CONSENT AND WILL NEVER BE ABLE TO. The schema anchor already notes that a third party never chose this filesystem; a dead subject is the limiting case, and the practical consequence is that no future consent can cure an exposure. The people who bear the harm are the survivors, who are named in the distribution schedule and did not choose the machine either. THIRD, ONE FILE IS A COMPLETE FINANCIAL X-RAY OF ONE HOUSEHOLD. 00's corpus sentence describes this file exactly - a collection "can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records" - and an estate file assembles the identity documents, every account statement, the tax position, sometimes the medical records that explain a death, the will, and the private family correspondence about it, all at once, deliberately, in one place, because assembling them is the job. Consequences the row commits to: (a) NO NAME MAY BECOME A FOLDER LEVEL - not the deceased, not the executor, not a beneficiary - and unlike the schema default this does not relax on user approval, because a path naming a dead person writes a bereavement into a filesystem the surviving family share, against "The default posture must therefore be local-first and data-minimizing."; the allocated file reference is the safe display label because it names nobody. (b) NO LEGAL STATUS IS EVER INFERRED - not validity, revocation, entitlement, solvency, tax liability, clearance, survivorship, or whether distribution is safe; the literal label is preserved as an observation. (c) SHARE AND VALUE FIGURES ARE NOT SUMMARISED OUT OF THE FILE - a preview line that reveals a residue figure or a beneficiary's share is the disclosure the file exists to control, which is the same shape as 00's warning that "A summary such as “11 protected identity records” may be safe to show, while a visible list of passport filenames on a shared screen may not be." (d) Where a model is needed on this content, "If a model needs text containing sensitive content, the user should see that requirement and choose whether to allow a local model, a cloud model, a redacted prompt, or no model use." This row does not carry is_safety_domain - 00's four are named and closed - but it co-activates three of them.
open_question: NJ-EA-1: the lay executor. A bereaved person administering a parent's estate personally produces every structural signal in this row and none of the practitioner precondition, so the file falls to legal.personal-legal-matters where the estate-specific signals - the valuation instant, the three-ledger accounts, the distribution shares - are invisible. Alternatives for R1c: (a) leave it, and accept that the commonest estate corpus in a consumer product is recognised only generically; (b) let legal.personal-legal-matters adopt this row's deterministic signals by reference, which keeps one row but splits its recognition across two schemas; (c) mint a personal-side sibling under legal, which this row does NOT propose because it would be a second copy of the same evidence. NJ-EA-2: the date of death has no canonical key and this row deliberately does not mint one - creation_date is wrong and tax_year is wrong. It may be that a death date is permanently EVIDENCE rather than a fact, in which case the anchor is `subject_of_record` alone and is weaker than this row assumes; R1c should say which. NJ-EA-3: whether a will trust arising on death is one file family or two - the first accounting period runs from the death date, so the administration and the continuing trust genuinely overlap, and the collision fixture in this row cannot be resolved from the design docs.
